Mox v0.8.0 adds direct session attachment, more command aliases, and local
session name inference while preserving explicit SSH host arguments.

### Commands

- Attach with `mox work`, `mox attach work`, or `mox a work`. Configured
  sessions are built when stopped; running unmanaged sessions can be attached
  by name. `mox -a work` continues to work.
- Added aliases: `e` for edit; `k` and `rm` for kill; `l` for list;
  `i` and `imp` for import; and `n` for new. The existing `ls` and `cssh`
  aliases remain.
- `mox new .` and `mox new ..` use the resolved directory's name for a local
  session. `mox new my-project -r ~/proj` names a local session in `~/proj`.
- A sole configured session name in `mox new` expands its hosts. Use
  `mox new -n scratch server1` to keep an explicit literal host, including
  when it matches a directory or configured session. `@cluster` expansion
  remains available with `-n`.

### Reliability

- Commands without dry-run support reject `--print`. Positional attachment,
  `attach`, and `new` print their tmux commands without executing them;
  `import --print` previews YAML without saving it.
- Explicitly named SSH sessions retain their hosts when `--root` is supplied.
- `-a` and `--attach` reject extra positional arguments instead of silently
  ignoring them. Config variables and trailing `key=value` overrides are
  not supported in this release.
- The named local session example now uses `mox new -n my-project`.

### Install or update

Download the archive for your OS and architecture below and verify it against
`checksums.txt`, or build the tagged version with Go 1.25 or newer:

```sh
go install github.com/bthall/mox/cmd/mox@v0.8.0
```

Runtime requires tmux 3.1 or newer. Existing configurations continue to work;
updating the binary does not require restarting running tmux sessions.
